categories.name: API clients
categories.description: Compose requests, inspect responses, and explore endpoints.

categories.name: Functional testing
categories.description: Validate REST behavior and maintain repeatable regression checks.

categories.name: Test generation
categories.description: Generate test inputs and explore behavior with automated mutations or fuzzing.

categories.name: Contract & schema
categories.description: Check consumer-provider agreements and OpenAPI response conformance.

categories.name: Security testing
categories.description: Assess authentication behavior, API vulnerabilities, and security controls.

categories.name: Performance
categories.description: Measure REST API response behavior, throughput, and load.

categories.name: Mocking
categories.description: Simulate HTTP services and isolate dependencies during testing.

categories.name: Monitoring
categories.description: Run scheduled REST API checks and alert on failures.

categories.name: Traffic recording & replay
categories.description: Capture HTTP traffic and replay it as repeatable regression tests or service mocks.

tools.name: Advanced REST Client
tools.description: A desktop HTTP client for composing REST requests, inspecting responses, and organizing reusable API requests.
tools.notes: This entry covers the ARC Electron desktop application. Current maintenance status and a dedicated CI runner have not been confirmed.

tools.name: Apidog
tools.description: Design and explore REST APIs, validate responses against schemas, build automated test scenarios, and simulate services with mocks.
features: OpenAPI-based API design and response validation
Chained test scenarios and data-driven runs
tools.notes: Free and paid plans are available. Hosted, local, and on-premises capabilities depend on the selected edition and execution mode.

tools.name: Bowire
tools.description: A multi-protocol API workbench with REST discovery, request assertions, traffic recording and replay, mocks, and command-line automation.
features: Recorded sessions, replay mocks, security scans, and latency measurements
tools.notes: Runs standalone or embedded in an ASP.NET application. Protocols use plugins; this entry describes its REST capabilities.

tools.name: Bruno
tools.description: A local, Git-friendly API client with file-based collections, scripted assertions, and a CLI runner.
tools.notes: Paid editions add features. The open-source license describes the core, not every commercial component.

tools.name: Chapar
tools.description: A local desktop REST client with file-based collections, Python scripts, chained test cases, and a CLI for repeatable API checks.
features: Python pre-request and response test scripts
Chained test cases and chapar-cli execution
tools.notes: Also supports other API protocols. Collections and environments are stored locally.

tools.name: Checkly
tools.description: Define REST API checks, run them on a schedule, and investigate failures with monitoring and alerting.
tools.notes: This entry describes the hosted monitoring service. Limits and capabilities vary by plan.

tools.name: EvoMaster
tools.description: Automatically generate and execute REST API tests using search-based fuzzing, then export reproducible regression tests.
features: Black-box and instrumented white-box API fuzzing
Stateful request sequences and fault detection
tools.notes: REST testing uses API schema information. White-box exploration additionally requires integration with the application under test.

tools.name: Firecamp
tools.description: A multi-protocol API client for exploring REST endpoints, organizing collections, inspecting responses, and collaborating on API requests.
tools.notes: The source repository is open source. Current hosted plan pricing, maintenance status, and CI runner availability have not been confirmed.

tools.name: Flowtest
tools.description: Build visual multi-step HTTP API tests, reuse values between requests, and monitor complete REST workflows with scheduled runs and alerts.
features: Hosted execution and local or private agents
tools.notes: Private-agent access, execution limits, and notification channels depend on the plan. A private agent does not imply a self-hosted control plane.

tools.name: Frisby
tools.description: A JavaScript REST API testing framework built on Jest, with fluent HTTP requests and assertions for status codes, JSON values, and types.
tools.notes: Tests run in a Node.js project using Jest; expected behavior is authored by the user.

tools.name: Hoppscotch
tools.description: An API development platform for exploring REST endpoints, organizing collections, scripting response checks, and running tests from a CLI.
features: CLI collection runs with JUnit reports
tools.notes: The community edition is MIT licensed; commercial editions have separate terms. A hosted workspace does not necessarily mean requests execute in the cloud.

tools.name: HTTPie
tools.description: A command-line HTTP client with readable request syntax, JSON support, sessions, and formatted output for exploring and debugging REST APIs.
features: Readable HTTP and JSON request syntax
tools.notes: This entry covers the open-source HTTPie CLI. HTTPie for Web and Desktop is a separate product with separate terms.

tools.name: Hurl
tools.description: Run HTTP requests and REST API assertions from plain-text files, with chained requests, captured values, and command-line test reports.
features: Plain-text HTTP request and assertion files

tools.name: Insomnia
tools.description: Explore REST endpoints, organize requests, write API tests, and execute collections from a desktop client or CLI.
tools.notes: Cloud collaboration and enterprise capabilities depend on the selected plan.

tools.name: k6
tools.description: A developer-oriented load testing tool for scripting HTTP workloads, measuring performance, and enforcing thresholds.
tools.notes: The local k6 engine is open source. Grafana Cloud k6 is a separate hosted offering.

tools.name: Karate
tools.description: A test automation framework for expressing REST requests, assertions, and multi-step API scenarios in a readable DSL.
features: API test reuse for performance workflows
tools.notes: Plugins and enterprise components have separate commercial terms.

tools.name: Keploy
tools.description: Capture REST API traffic and dependency interactions, generate tests and mocks, and replay them against new builds to detect regressions.
features: Local and CI replay with response comparison
tools.notes: The local record-and-replay core is open source. Hosted AI generation and enterprise capabilities have separate limits and terms.

tools.name: Kreya
tools.description: A desktop REST API client with local project files, scripted assertions, response snapshots, and a headless CLI for automated checks.
tools.notes: Testing, scripting, snapshot, and CLI capabilities depend on the selected plan. Also supports other API protocols.

tools.name: Pact
tools.description: Consumer-driven contract testing for HTTP integrations, verifying that consumers and providers agree on API interactions.
tools.notes: Pact is an ecosystem of implementations. License details vary; hosted commercial contract services are outside this entry.

tools.name: PactumJS
tools.description: A JavaScript REST API testing library for end-to-end, integration, component, and contract checks, with HTTP mocks and reusable test steps.
features: Fluent REST request and response assertions
tools.notes: PactumJS and Pact are separate projects. This entry describes the Node.js PactumJS library.

tools.name: Parasoft SOAtest
tools.description: Automate REST API and integration tests using visual workflows, traffic-derived test generation, data-driven scenarios, and CI execution.
features: Visual data-driven REST and integration tests
Tests generated from recorded API traffic
tools.notes: Feature availability depends on licensed components. Parasoft Virtualize is a separate product; its capabilities are not attributed to SOAtest here.

tools.name: Pororoca
tools.description: A desktop HTTP API client with collections, environments, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 support, and a .NET library for automated REST checks.
tools.license: GPL-3.0-or-later notice with additional project restrictions
tools.notes: The repository adds restrictions on commercial derivatives with server-syncing features to its GPL notice. Automated tests use Pororoca.Test and a .NET test runner.

tools.name: Portman
tools.description: Generate Postman collections and REST API contract, variation, and integration tests from OpenAPI specifications, then run them with Newman.
tools.notes: Requires an OpenAPI specification. Generated tests are Postman collections; execution uses Newman.

tools.name: Posting
tools.description: A terminal-based HTTP API client for composing REST requests, inspecting responses, and versioning local request collections as YAML files.
tools.notes: The cli interface denotes an interactive terminal UI. A dedicated unattended assertion runner has not been confirmed.

tools.name: Postman
tools.description: An API development platform for composing REST requests, organizing collections, and running scripted tests and monitors.
tools.notes: Availability, collaboration, and execution limits vary by plan. A free plan does not make the product open source.

tools.name: ReadyAPI
tools.description: A commercial API testing platform for REST functional scenarios, automated security scans, performance workloads, and service virtualization.
features: Visual and scripted REST test scenarios
Security scans and reusable performance tests
REST service virtualization and CI integration
tools.notes: Functional, performance, virtualization, and execution capabilities depend on the purchased ReadyAPI components. SoapUI Open Source has its own entry.

tools.name: Rentgen
tools.description: Generate and execute REST API discovery tests from a working cURL request, covering invalid inputs, boundaries, HTTP behavior, and security checks.
tools.notes: Official binaries are free, including for internal commercial use. Source-code use has RSAL-1.0 restrictions. Maintained by the team behind REST Atlas.

tools.name: REST Assured
tools.description: A Java library for writing expressive REST API tests with HTTP requests, response assertions, and reusable test code.
tools.notes: Requires a Java-based test project. Test scenarios and expected outcomes are authored by the user.

tools.name: RESTler
tools.description: A stateful REST API fuzzer that derives request dependencies from OpenAPI specifications and generates sequences to find security and reliability faults.
tools.notes: Requires an OpenAPI specification and configuration for the target service. Testing cloud APIs does not make the fuzzer a hosted service.

tools.name: Schemathesis
tools.description: Generate property-based REST API tests from OpenAPI schemas to find server errors, invalid-input behavior, and response conformance issues.
tools.notes: REST testing requires an OpenAPI specification. The entry covers the open-source test runner.

tools.name: SoapUI
tools.description: An open-source desktop application for REST API functional tests, response assertions, security scans, load tests, and HTTP service mocks.
features: REST request steps and response assertions
Security scans and basic load testing
HTTP mocking and command-line test execution
tools.notes: This entry covers SoapUI Open Source. ReadyAPI is a separate commercial platform with additional automation and reporting capabilities.

tools.name: Swagger UI
tools.description: An interactive, OpenAPI-powered REST API explorer for sending requests, supplying authentication, and inspecting live responses directly in a browser.
features: Interactive API documentation generated from OpenAPI
Try it out requests with parameters, bodies, and authentication
Live response status, headers, and body inspection
tools.notes: Requires an OpenAPI definition. This entry covers the open-source Swagger UI component; commercial Swagger products have separate plans and capabilities.

tools.name: Tavern
tools.description: Define REST API test scenarios in YAML and run them with pytest, with chained stages, response validation, and Python extensions.
features: Declarative YAML request and response tests
pytest integration and Python custom validation
tools.notes: Also supports other protocols. This entry covers its REST API testing workflow.

tools.name: Thunder Client
tools.description: A REST API client inside VS Code and JetBrains editors, with local collections, visual response assertions, and a CLI for automated runs.
features: Local collections and CLI collection runs
tools.notes: The free tier has limits. CLI and CI/CD execution require a paid plan. Announced performance testing is not counted as an available capability.

tools.name: WireMock
tools.description: Create controllable HTTP service doubles to test REST integrations without relying on live downstream dependencies.
tools.notes: The open-source server and WireMock Cloud have different deployment options and terms.

tools.name: Yaak
tools.description: A local-first REST API client with desktop and command-line interfaces, request chaining, environments, and Git-friendly workspace files.
features: Desktop and CLI access to the same requests
tools.notes: Source code is MIT licensed. Official prebuilt binaries are free for personal use; work use requires a commercial license after the trial.

tools.name: ZAP
tools.description: A dynamic security testing tool with HTTP inspection, automated scanning, and API scanning workflows for REST services.
tools.notes: Configure authentication and API definitions for the target. Scan only systems you are authorized to test.
